description: SpectraShift is a software development team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to make astronomical data more accessible through an interactive web platform that helps users explore SPHEREx observations, compare images of the same region of the sky over time, and identify objects that move or change in brightness. By combining intuitive design with real space data, we hope to make astronomical discovery easier for researchers, students, and space enthusiasts.
summary: ORBITAL is an independent browser-based workspace that makes astronomical data easier to explore and understand. Users can search released SPHEREx archive records, preview images, browse reference fields, compare observations, and save research notes. Educational tools introduce concepts such as parallax while keeping data sources and scientific limitations clear. By bringing discovery, comparison, and learning together, ORBITAL makes astronomical exploration more accessible without presenting illustrative content as scientific discoveries.
details:
ORBITAL - Project Details

Github: https://github.com/baziedy/orbital

ORBITAL is an independent educational prototype inspired by the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge context. Its Explore workspace searches NASA/IPAC IRSA for released SPHEREx archive records and available FITS products, while also presenting curated STScI Digitized Sky Survey (DSS) reference images for selected practice targets.

Users can inspect metadata and image previews, compare views using slider, blink, and side-by-side modes, explore sky layers through CDS Aladin Lite, and maintain browser-local research notes with text export. Additional tools demonstrate idealized parallax and orbital relationships, coordinate offsets, image marking, and illustrative spectral sonification.

The interface is built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Sass, and Recharts. Its service layer uses FastAPI, Python, Astropy, and Pillow. ORBITAL combines archive access with a guided visual-review workflow, using explicit source labels to distinguish scientific data from reference imagery and educational illustrations.

The platform also communicates important scientific limitations. Curated DSS dates are illustrative; image comparisons are not WCS-registered or calibrated; generated spectral curves are not measured spectra; and the simulator is not a detection or orbit-fitting system. Research notes are stored locally in the user's browser.

ORBITAL is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA or NASA Space Apps. NASA does not endorse any non-U.S. Government entity and is not responsible for information contained on non-U.S. Government websites.
